title: Choose Docfold's visual world
question: The roll assigned Airmail Post. Keep it, take the alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Airmail Post
options.lineage: Airmail envelopes, postage stamp sheets, and postmark cancellations
options.thesis: Every document is a letter you seal on the phone and send only when you choose.
options.viewport: Home: chevron-banded top bar with the date span in view, documents as envelopes each carrying its own stamp colour and a giant page-count numeral, one Scan FAB, banner ad parked on the bottom edge.
options.risk: Turns into a costume if the stamps and postmarks leak into controls instead of staying on pages and moments.

raised.raise: Hierarchy by scale contrast alone: giant page numerals against tiny mono labels, no badges or boxes doing that job.
The stamp-sheet organizer packs 3 pages per row on a phone with hairline gutters; nothing wastes a pixel.
Guide words: the home top bar names the first and last date in view, recomputed as you scroll.
A visible capacity: export shows the PDF size against upload limits (500 KB, 1 MB, 2 MB) and compresses to fit.
One ribbon colour per document: its stamp colour follows it everywhere it appears.
Page state is a mark on the stamp (crop corner, filter dot, rotation tick), not a chip.

options.label: Copy Shop Riso
options.lineage: The photocopy shop counter and two-colour risograph print
options.thesis: The app is the copy shop in your pocket: toner black, fluorescent inks, the light bar sweeping the glass.
options.viewport: Home: an oversized two-ink wordmark offset by misregistration, documents as copier output stacks, a Scan FAB that triggers a light-bar sweep.
options.risk: Riso and zine styling is a familiar indie look, and halftone textures cost frames on low-end phones if not drawn with care.

options.label: Variable Font Specimen
options.thesis: A page count drawn as one giant morphing glyph.
options.viewport: A giant numeral per document with a weight axis.
options.case: Loses both axes: a scanner user does not identify with type specimens, and the slider has no scanning job.
options.risk: Reads as a font demo, not a tool.

options.label: Labanotation Score
options.thesis: Pages as shaped blocks on a vertical staff.
options.viewport: A centre staff of pages read upward.
options.case: Loses both axes: no audience recognition and the upward staff fights a page list.
options.kept: State encoded by mark shape and fill, not by labels.

options.label: Character Goods Catalog
options.thesis: Each document as a mascot with a name plate.
options.case: Loses both axes: too toy-like for ID cards and certificates.
options.kept: One ribbon colour per item, carried everywhere it appears.

options.label: High-Density Web
options.thesis: Every document and tool packed into one ruled mosaic.
options.case: Loses both axes: hurried, low-literacy users need fewer, larger targets.
options.kept: Density courage and a strict hairline grid in the page organizer.

options.label: Lexicon Shoulder & Plate
options.thesis: Documents as entries with colour only inside plates.
options.viewport: A text column of documents with guide words.
options.case: Loses both axes: bookish and slow for an urgent one-minute task.
options.kept: Guide words naming the first and last item in view.

options.label: Cassette J-Card
options.thesis: Documents as folded inlays with a spine title.
options.viewport: Spine-only list that unfolds into pages.
options.case: Loses both axes: cassettes are foreign to most of the audience in 2026.
options.kept: A hard capacity made visible: the size budget on export.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: What Adobe Scan and the Drive scanner ship, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Top app bar, recent documents as thumbnail rows, a blue camera FAB.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the competition by design.
